It's math all the way down and each activity needs to be separately evaluated. I motorcycle, and have for 30 years. I speed, digitally pirate, have sex... Lots of stuff. It's like this:

If the chance of ultimate failure (permanent injury, jail / prison, death, et cetera) is high enough there's an uncontrollable likelihood of such a thing happening, then the activity may not be worth it. This risk is of course mitigated by intelligence and experience and all that, but in certain cases mitigation may not help.

For me, skydiving is such an activity. There's a relatively low risk of injury. However, a fuck up will usually result in death and will very likely not be within the sky diver's control.

On the other hand, motorcycling is an inherently dangerous activity moment to moment. Some fuck ups can result in death or permanent injury, but most don't. However, experience and careful riding (read: somewhat paranoid) can help tremendously.

Finally, some activities have a pay-off. Commuting via motorcycle saves me about $7,000 per year over driving my car. That's money. It saves me about $1,000 and lots and lots of time over public transit. So that has to be considered.
